$comment:
The catalogue this repository publishes, so a consumer gets the language server by name instead of by path: `claude plugin marketplace add ecoma-io/archkeep`, then `claude plugin install archkeep@archkeep`. It is at the repository root rather than under `.claude/`, because a marketplace added from GitHub is read from the default branch's root and a catalogue hidden inside an agent's own config directory would be found by this repository's sessions and by nobody else's.

A session in THIS repository reads it too, but not by finding it — publishing a catalogue registers nothing, and a session that is merely near this file has no idea it exists. `../.claude/settings.json` is what registers it, as a `directory` marketplace at the repository root, and that entry is the whole reason the arrangement worth naming holds: the plugin runs from the same working tree as the code it acts on, so a change to the server is exercised by the pull request that makes it, with no published version for a session here to be behind. Registration was missing for as long as this note claimed otherwise, and every session here ran without the plugin, silently.

This file lists what the repository OFFERS. `.claude/settings.json` decides what a session here USES, and the two are deliberately not the same set. `packages/archkeep/src/conformance/plugin-catalogue.integration.test.mjs` holds both halves to what they can each be checked against: every entry here against the manifest it points at, and every plugin those settings enable against the marketplace they name.

Claude Code ignores manifest keys it does not know (`claude plugin validate` says so in as many words), which is where this note lives.
